question.text: Krishna Mezzanine Fund (Cat II) holds unlisted NCDs of a portfolio company for 30 months and redeems them on 15 November 2024 at a gain of INR 6 crore, pass-through to resident LP Mr. Sanjay Raghavan. Given Finance (No.2) Act 2024 amendments, how is this gain characterised and taxed?

answer.text: Long-term capital gain taxable at 12.5% (since held >24 months).
Long-term capital gain taxable at 20% with indexation.

DEEMED short-term capital gain (irrespective of holding period) taxable at the LP's applicable slab rates — because unlisted debentures transferred/redeemed on or after 23-07-2024 are deemed short-term capital assets.
Exempt, as debentures are interest-bearing instruments.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The Finance (No.2) Act 2024 amended the rules so that capital gains on REDEMPTION or TRANSFER of UNLISTED debentures on or after 23-07-2024 are DEEMED to be short-term capital gains, irrespective of holding period. Hence even though held 30 months, Mr. Raghavan's INR 6 crore gain is STCG taxed at applicable slab rates (with surcharge and cess — LTCG surcharge cap does NOT apply as this is slab-taxed income). **The Trap:** Option A wrongly treats unlisted debentures as normal LT capital assets. Option B applies the pre-Budget 2024 rate AND indexation (both have been removed). Option D ignores the chapter's clear statement that redemption gains on unlisted debentures are capital gains, not interest. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same deemed-STCG rule. The same rule was introduced for Market Linked Debentures (MLDs) in FA 2023, and extended to ALL unlisted debentures in FA 2024. XXI-B (PMS) encounters it for debt mandates. Specified Mutual Funds (SMFs) acquired on/after 1 April 2023 are similarly deemed STCG. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For Cat II debt funds, this rule materially shifts LP after-tax IRR — a 40% slab LP now pays ~40% vs the 12.5% LTCG rate previously available for >36-month holdings. Re-price your coupon expectations and update your LP after-tax IRR decks; this could be a material disclosure at the next LP annual meeting.
